issues.description: Changelog claims 'real-time pacing' but the diff only chunks bytes with no pacing logic.
issues.detail: The new buffer drains in a tight while-loop and emits full packets back-to-back, with no link to _send_interval/_next_send_time. Either wire actual pacing into the buffer or remove the 'real-time pacing' claim from the changelog. Shipping docs that overstate behavior is worse than shipping a smaller feature.

issues.description: Packetization buffer mutates any binary payload and leaks serializer framing into a generic transport.
issues.detail: fixed_audio_packet_size triggers on any bytes payload, so non-audio binary control messages would be chopped into PCM-sized chunks. Wire framing is a property of the Vonage protocol, not of FastAPIWebsocketTransport. Gate on AudioRawFrame or move packetization into the serializer (or a small pure packetizer it composes).

issues.description: Buffer has no stated invariant, no input validation, and ordering hazards across payload types.
issues.detail: Zero or negative fixed_audio_packet_size causes infinite loop or misbehavior; odd values split PCM samples mid-frame. The buffer is place-oriented mutable state shared across _write_frame and process_frame with no stated FIFO invariant, so non-bytes payloads can overtake buffered audio. Validate >0, document the byte-count formula, and model as a value-returning packetizer.

issues.description: Tail audio is never flushed; final partial packet is silently dropped at end-of-stream.
issues.detail: Remainder bytes sit in _audio_send_buffer until another audio frame arrives that pushes it over threshold. On EndFrame/CancelFrame or long silences the trailing sub-packet is discarded with no log or pad-and-flush. Either flush on stream termination or document the drop explicitly.

issues.description: DTMF parsing accepts two undocumented shapes on speculation rather than a cited Vonage contract.
issues.detail: deserialize() reads digit from message['digit'] or message['dtmf']['digit'] with no link to Vonage docs. Pick the shape Vonage actually sends, cite it in a comment, and delete the other branch. Defensive 'try both shapes' code rots into permanent ambiguity nobody dares remove.

issues.description: No tests for the serializer or packetization buffer, including the chunk-boundary math.
issues.detail: New protocol serializer, new stateful transport buffer, interruption-clear behavior, and remainder handling all ship untested. The 640-byte = 20ms @ 16kHz PCM16 math is exactly the off-by-one that surfaces months later. Add unit tests covering odd-sized payloads, chunk boundaries, and interruption-clears-buffer semantics.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the Vonage serializer itself is mostly correct but under-specified, while the new fixed_audio_packet_size buffer in FastAPIWebsocketTransport is the consequential and under-baked part of the diff. Three independent concerns converge: the changelog overstates 'real-time pacing' the code does not implement; the buffer indiscriminately chunks any binary payload and leaks Vonage's wire framing into a generic transport; and the buffer lacks stated invariants, input validation, tail-flush behavior, and tests. The DTMF dual-shape parsing is a smaller but unanimous taste issue. NEEDS-WORK: deliver pacing or drop the claim, gate/relocate packetization, validate inputs, flush tails, cite the DTMF contract, and add tests.
